title: AIDA
subtitle: AI-Driven Distributed Autonomy
summary: Connecting vehicle dynamics, learning and distributed decision-making across autonomous vehicles.
body: AIDA investigates distributed learning and coordination for connected autonomous vehicles. The project brings together recurrent neural networks and state-space models, model predictive control, reinforcement learning and language-assisted planning.

The research connects small-scale RoboRacer experiments with vehicle-dynamics modeling and validation. It is led by Agnes Poks at TU Wien, with scientific collaboration across Technical Dynamics and Vehicle System Dynamics and Cyber-Physical Systems.
The project plan covers November 2026 to April 2029. The public FWF record lists grant PAT3743226; the research is presented here as funded work, without claiming completed outcomes.

title: ADEX
subtitle: Autonomous-Driving Examiner
summary: A historical autonomous-driving research project connecting scenario generation, formal task specifications and safe learning.
body: ADEX — Autonomous-Driving Examiner — ran from 2020 to 2024 with support from the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG).

The TU Wien research record connects ADEX to work on scenario-based curriculum generation for multi-agent driving, hierarchical potential-based reward shaping and safe policy improvement. Related racing research was also acknowledged in the report on the 2021 Grand Prix victory.
The publications and demonstration below preserve these research outputs. The separate curriculum and reward-shaping pages provide a closer look at individual lines of work.
imageCaption: Figure 1 · HPRS: hierarchical potential-based reward shaping from task specifications

title: Unit XIII
subtitle: Our next generation of autonomous race cars
imageCaption: Unit XIII autonomous racing project logo
summary: Building an autonomous race car on the 1:8 Serpent SRX8GTE R platform, alongside simulation work in RoboRacer Arena.
body: Unit XIII is our new autonomous race car build based on the Serpent SRX8GTE R (SER600074), a 1:8 electric GT chassis with four-wheel drive.

The current build plan pairs a Hobbywing Xerun 4268SD G3 2400 KV motor with a VESC 6 Mk6 HP controller. The planned sensor package includes a RoboSense Airy LiDAR, a MicroStrain IMU and a ground-facing Holybro H-Flow. Onboard compute is still being evaluated between an ASUS NUC 15 Pro and an NVIDIA Jetson.
RoboRacer Arena is the simulation theme within Unit XIII. It turns validated track maps into Isaac Sim environments and connects experiments in simulation with tests on the physical racing platform.

title: RoboRacer Arena
subtitle: Specification-driven track construction for autonomous racing
summary: A pipeline connecting track requirements to validated maps, Isaac Sim environments and evaluation on the physical racing platform.
body: RoboRacer Arena treats track geometry as an experimental variable. The pipeline turns requirements into closed-loop layouts, validates occupancy maps and generates simulation assets.
The research connects a reference collection of 130 tracks with Isaac Sim environments and a reconstructed vehicle asset. It supports policy training and evaluation across different track geometries.

The 2026 preprint by Mihaela-Larisa Clement, Agnes Poks and Ezio Bartocci reports both simulation and physical-vehicle experiments. It was submitted to ICRA 2027; this page does not present it as an accepted conference paper.

title: Latent Imagination
subtitle: Learning to race before meeting the real track
summary: Model-based reinforcement learning and zero-shot transfer from simulation to a physical racing car.
body: Latent Imagination studies how an autonomous racing policy can learn using a compact model of its environment, then transfer to a physical vehicle without additional training on the real track.
The work links a learned latent world model with actor–critic learning. The published ICRA 2022 paper and the accompanying demonstration document the approach and its transfer to autonomous racing.
The archive includes the original research video, a paper presentation and the preceding master’s thesis on model-based deep reinforcement learning.

title: Learning from Human Attention
subtitle: Where a driver looks, and what an agent learns
summary: Human-attention feature maps for robot learning, object detection and autonomous racing.
body: This research explores learned human-attention feature maps as an input to robot learning. It asks how information about visually relevant regions can help autonomous agents.

The 2023 workshop paper is accompanied by three completed master’s theses: attention-based driving agents, dynamic object detection for autonomous multi-agent systems, and attention-based autonomous racing.
Together, these outputs document a line of work connecting perception and learning to the racing platform.

title: Depth Matters
subtitle: Multimodal perception for autonomous agents
summary: Combining color and depth for robust autonomous driving, with deployment on resource-constrained platforms.
body: Depth Matters studies multimodal RGB-D perception for autonomous agents. The work combines visual appearance and depth information and investigates robustness in learned controllers.

A companion workshop paper addresses deployment of RGB-D multimodal controllers on resource-constrained platforms. Mihaela-Larisa Clement’s 2025 master’s thesis documents the development of multimodal RGB-D driving agents.
Subsequent research investigates how liquid neural networks generalize when the driving environment changes. Papers, thesis and workshop records are linked below.
imageCaption: Figure 1 · Depth Matters: Multimodal RGB-D Perception for Robust Autonomous Agents

title: Learning-Based MPC
subtitle: Learned dynamics. Predictive control.
summary: Recurrent neural models of vehicle dynamics as a basis for nonlinear model predictive control.
body: This research connects recurrent neural network modeling with nonlinear model predictive control. It studies how learned dynamics can support autonomous driving while accounting for the demands of predictive control.

The 2026 preprint Towards Safe Learning-Based Non-Linear Model Predictive Control through Recurrent Neural Network Modeling documents this line of work. A related completed thesis studies system dynamics in partially observable environments with biologically inspired recurrent networks.
The Scuderia MPC and vehicle-dynamics activities connect learning-based models with physical vehicles and track experiments.

title: Adaptive Recurrent Control
subtitle: Controllers that keep learning
summary: Real-time recurrent reinforcement learning and online fine-tuning of pretrained autonomous driving controllers.
body: Real-time recurrent reinforcement learning addresses adaptation in sequential decision-making. In autonomous driving, the research investigates online fine-tuning of pretrained controllers.
The work is documented in an AAAI 2025 paper, a 2026 driving preprint and a workshop contribution at ICLR 2026. The records distinguish published proceedings, workshop papers and preprints.
imageCaption: Figure 1 · Adaptive Control in Autonomous Driving via Real-Time Recurrent RL

title: Learning Adaptive Safety
subtitle: Safety in multi-agent environments
summary: Learning safety-aware behavior in multi-agent systems, with a research demonstration and open paper.
body: Learning Adaptive Safety for Multi-Agent Systems studies the relationship between learning, safety and interactions with other agents.
The ICRA 2024 work is documented in the linked paper and research video. A related workshop contribution considers safe learning under assumptions in human–robot systems.
imageCaption: Figure 1 · Learning Adaptive Safety for Multi-Agent Systems

title: Multi-Agent Driving Curricula
subtitle: Learning from increasingly challenging scenarios
summary: Scenario-based curriculum generation for multi-agent driving.
body: Scenario-Based Curriculum Generation for Multi-Agent Driving studies how training scenarios can be organized to support learning in interactive driving environments.
The ICRA 2025 paper links autonomous driving, curriculum learning and multi-agent systems. The source record associates this work with the ADEX project (2020–2024).
imageCaption: Figure 1 · Scenario-Based Curriculum Generation for Multi-Agent Driving

title: HPRS
subtitle: Reward shaping from task specifications
summary: Hierarchical potential-based reward shaping for learning agents, with an original demonstration.
body: HPRS explores how task specifications can guide reinforcement learning through hierarchical potential-based reward shaping.

The archive connects the original demonstration to the publication listed in the author-maintained bibliography. A separate 2022 paper studies safe policy improvement in constrained Markov decision processes.
imageCaption: Figure 1 · HPRS: hierarchical potential-based reward shaping from task specifications

title: MMDVS-LF
subtitle: Dynamic vision meets human attention
summary: A multimodal dynamic vision sensor and eye-tracking dataset for line following.
body: MMDVS-LF documents a multimodal dataset combining dynamic vision sensing and eye tracking for line following.
The work connects event-based perception and human visual attention with autonomous agent research. The linked preprint provides the dataset description and experimental context.

title: Liquid Neural Networks
subtitle: Bio-inspired models for sequential decision-making
summary: From neural circuit policies and liquid time-constant networks to scalable liquid-resistance and liquid-capacitance models.
body: This collection brings together the bio-inspired neural network research that informs autonomous-agent work around Scuderia Segfault.

The archive includes Neural Circuit Policies, Liquid Time-Constant Networks, research on chemical and electrical synapses, and liquid-resistance/liquid-capacitance models. More recent preprints investigate efficient sequence modeling and state-space models.
These are related research outputs rather than a single funded project. Each publication retains its own year, source and publication type.
imageCaption: Figure 1 · Liquid Resistance Liquid Capacitance Networks

title: NimbleAI
subtitle: Neuromorphic sensing and processing at the endpoint
summary: A related Cyber-Physical Systems project on energy-efficient neuromorphic sensing and processing.
body: NimbleAI is a related Cyber-Physical Systems research project on ultra-energy-efficient and secure neuromorphic sensing and processing at the endpoint. The TU Wien project record lists the period 2022–2026.

Felix Resch and Radu Grosu are among the authors of the DATE 2023 publication NimbleAI: Towards Neuromorphic Sensing-Processing 3D-integrated Chips. This page connects that documented contribution to the wider research context of event-based sensing.
The photograph shows the Scuderia racing platform as context; it is not presented as a NimbleAI project deliverable.
